newsitem.title: USA: Fox/Liberty buys stake in Madison Square Garden.
newsitem.headline: Fox/Liberty buys stake in Madison Square Garden.

text.p: Fox/Liberty Networks has agreed to buy a 40 percent stake in New York's Madison Square Garden arena and related sports franchises for $850 million in a bid to create a new national sports network, the companies said Monday.

Fox's venture with Rainbow Media Holdings Inc., which will include national, regional and local sports programming reaching 55 million homes under the name Fox Sports Net, is meant to create an alternative to rival ESPN, officials said.
It will appear on nine Fox/Liberty cable channels, eight Rainbow channels, and the Fox Sports regional sports networks.
Rainbow will maintain management control of its current regional sports networks, but they will be rebranded under the Fox Sports banner, with the exception of MSG Network and SportsChannel Florida.
Rainbow will also maintain management control of Madison Square Garden, including the New York Knicks basketball team and the New York Rangers ice hockey team.
Fox and Rainbow will share equally in advertising revenues and have an equal say on the programming of Fox Sports Net.

"This is a major step in providing a real national sports network under the Fox name with Fox quality," said Rupert Murdoch, chief executive of News Corp., which owns the Fox TV network. "Viewers will now have Fox Sports programming on a local and national level, which viewers have long desired."
The deal strengthens the cable businesses of Rainbow's owners -- Cablevision Systems Corp., with a 75 percent stake, and General Electric Co.'s NBC unit, with 25 percent.
Cablevision Chief Executive James Dolan said the deal "represents a significant step forward in Cablevision's overall financial strategy of reducing leverage and focusing on our core businesses."

The venture will sell national advertising slots on the regional channels and national programmes. The service, for the first time, provides advertisers with an easy way to buy time on dozens of local sports broadcasts, they said.
In addition, the new American Sports Classics network will be operated as a 50/50 partnership, managed by Fox/Liberty.

Fox/Liberty said it will raise the $850 million through a bank loan. Fox/Liberty is a joint venture of News Corp.'s Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp. Liberty Media is a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
Cablevision will use the proceeds to pay down $1.1 billion in debt that Rainbow assumed from buying the Madison Square Garden arena and related businesses in New York.
"Most of the proceeds is going to be used to pay down debt," Cablevision Vice Chairman Marc Lustgarten said.
He told reporters the deal was an alternative for national advertisers on the ESPN all-sports cable network, which is jointly owned by Walt Disney Co. and Hearst Corp.
"Fox/Liberty had one-half of an (advertising) dollar bill, and we had one half," Lustgarten said. "Now we're uniting, and that one dollar turns into 10 dollars."
He shied away from projecting how much in revenues the new Fox/Liberty-Rainbow ventures would generate for Cablevision. But he said the new venture "should create a great deal more cash flow."

Cablevision agreed in April to buy out ITT Corp.'s 50 percent partnership in Madison Square Garden, which includes the basketball and hockey teams and the MSG televison network. The companies teamed up in 1995 to buy the garden for $1 billion.
Separately, Cablevision said Lustgarten was named chairman of the board of Madison Square Garden. Fox/Liberty will have no management role in the MSG entities.
Cablevision stock rose 25 cents to $53.375 on the American Stock Exchange at midday. TCI fell 19 cents to $16.69 on Nasdaq. News Corp. added 37.5 cents to $19.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
